ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy sha 997d9970c437 (2026-05-05T08:45:37Z) updated the Go middleware dependency in frontend/middleware/buffer.go. The updated version introduced a regression in responseBufferMiddleware.ServeHTTP (line 87): after a client disconnects (HTTP 499), the middleware allocates a response buffer from the pool but never checks context cancellation (ctx.Done()) before or after the upstream fetch. The buffer is held in memory for the lifetime of the goroutine, which waits indefinitely for the upstream API response even after the client is gone. Under high traffic with any upstream latency, this leaks thousands of 64KB buffers, exhausting heap memory and causing an OOMKill within ~10 minutes.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately restart frontend pods to restore service (buys ~10 minutes before memory re-exhausts). 2. Roll back deploy 997d9970c437 by reverting frontend/go.mod, frontend/go.sum, and frontend/middleware/buffer.go to their state at sha 974792d4cdda, then redeploy. 3. Long-term fix: add a context cancellation check in responseBufferMiddleware.ServeHTTP — after client disconnect is detected via ctx.Done(), call bufferPool.Put(buf) and return immediately without waiting for the upstream response. Add a test case simulating client disconnects under slow upstream conditions.
